Karen — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front:

- Telemetry sources: Availability and latency are computed from two primary sources we provide: 1) production ingress edge proxies (real client requests routed to Redwood front-ends) and 2) our controlled synthetic probe fleet. For availability SLOs the authoritative source is production edge metrics; synthetic probes are used for validation and anomaly detection, not as the primary measurement for credits unless explicitly agreed in the contract.
- Aggregation & percentiles: Latency SLOs are expressed as p50/p95/p99 measured on successful requests over the rolling 30-day window. Availability is computed as the percentage of successful health-checked requests from the production edge over the same rolling 30-day window, sampled at 1-minute granularity by default. Regional SLOs can be scoped per-region; global commitments are computed as traffic-weighted aggregates across regions.
- Service credit calculation (example):
  Formula (monthly): credit_percentage = min( (SLO_target - observed_availability) / SLO_target, cap_pct )
  Example: Contracted availability = 99.95% (SLO_target). Observed availability for month = 99.65%.
  delta = 99.95 - 99.65 = 0.30 percentage points
  credit_percentage = 0.30 / 99.95 ≈ 0.003000 -> 0.30% of monthly committed fees (subject to cap). If your monthly committed spend is $120,000, credit = $360. Cap: as negotiated in contract (typical cap = 50% of monthly recurring fees for repeated major failures).
- Evidence and format: We will provide an evidence bundle that includes: timestamped production-edge samples (CSV), synthetic probe logs (parquet), and an audit appendix describing collection pipeline and sample SQL. We can deliver via secure Drive link or SFTP; typical formats: CSV (for immediate inspection) and Parquet for bulk archives.

Technical appendix (attach as PDF):
- Definitions:
  • Production edge: our front-line load-balanced proxies that terminate customer requests — includes request success/fail, latency_ms, region, and request_id.
  • Successful request: HTTP 2xx responses from the model-serving path (excluding cached prefix hits depending on contract).
- Sampling cadence: 1-minute aggregated buckets per instance; per-request telemetry retained for 30 days before aggregation retention policy applies.
- Measurement window: rolling 30-day window aligned to UTC calendar by default; can be aligned to billing cycle on request.
- Aggregation method: compute per-minute success_rate, then compute availability as (sum(successful_minutes) / total_minutes) * 100 over the window. For latency percentiles we compute per-request percentiles from the request sample, then roll up to window percentiles using weighted aggregation.
- Dispute process: we provide raw timestamps and hashes for a sample subset on request; we also support on-site or third-party audit for enterprise contracts.

Attachments included in evidence bundle: Redwood_SLO_Metrics_Definitions_v2.pdf (technical appendix), Telemetry_Schema.csv (sample CSV with column headers), Mutual_Action_Plan_Globex_Redwood.docx (delivery milestones).
